title: The Wednesday Tesh Mbaabu Wrote RejaReja's Closing Chapter
conflicts: Merchants: TechCabal says over 1 million; Mbaabu's own post and TechCrunch say over 270,000 (used). Markets: TechCrunch (Oct 2023) lists RejaReja discontinued in Kenya, Nigeria, Rwanda and Tanzania under a 'three markets' headline; TechTrends Kenya quotes Mbaabu that MarketForce was still operational in Kenya and Uganda. The story says it left Nigeria, Rwanda and Tanzania and that, per TechCrunch, RejaReja itself continued only in Uganda. Funding: $40 million Series A announced, $8 million of equity never wired (Mbaabu to TechCrunch); TechCrunch's $42.5 million total is not used. Chpter: TechCrunch calls it a spinout; Mbaabu says it was founded in 2021 by others whom he and Sibuti had backed; the story follows Mbaabu.
notes: Mbaabu's own closure post (teshmbaabu.com, 17 April 2024) loads and is the main source; four short quotations from it are used. The Pezesha credit dispute reported by TechCabal is left out because it was settled privately. The Founder Africa write-up was not used (promotional tone). Mbaabu's blog bio now names a later company (Cloud9 Money), outside this episode.
